blocks.title: Hero Background Image
blocks.css:
On the home page #first_container is the hero only, but it exists on every page: homepage-only CSS goes in updatePageCss without seo_id (printed after the Design Settings stylesheet and the sitewide Additional CSS). Photo: #first_container background-image; overlay: its inset box-shadow. Decorate with #first_container::after (the mobile preloader uses ::before) plus #first_container > .container{position:relative;z-index:1}. Hero padding (custom_164 / custom_165) is on #first_container .homepage_settings, so phone-only spacing is one @media rule. A background video behind the whole hero is one site widget named "Bootstrap Theme - Homepage Search - Extra Content Above" (createWidget, or add to it when the overview lists it under hero_site_widgets; it prints inside the hero on every hero type except Blank and the maps). The Homepage prints this widget by itself, whatever the hero widget contains and also when the hero widget is a site copy, so the hero widget is not edited. Video markup, CSS or script already in the hero widget (an earlier attempt) shows as a second video or does nothing: remove it from the hero widget, do not complete it.. Save these three fields as written, they are measured: the script moves the layer out of the content column to be the first child of #first_container, so the video fills the hero, the tint sits on the video, and the headline, form and buttons stay above both. A video file is shown at once, with no fade. Only a YouTube frame is held back: YouTube draws its title and a previous / pause / next overlay for a few seconds each time playback starts, also at every loop restart, and no URL parameter removes them, so the script shows the YouTube frame 5 seconds after it starts and hides it for the last second and a half before each restart, dissolving over 1.2 seconds. While the frame is hidden a visitor sees the hero behind it (its photo when custom_77 is on, otherwise its background colour) under the same tint as the video: the tint is on the layer, which is always visible, and the CSS turns the hero's own overlay off (box-shadow:none) so the photo and the video are never tinted differently. Leave custom_77 and custom_76 as they are unless the user asks. The frame is sized from the hero's own box, so it also covers a hero taller than the screen. widget_data for a video file:
widget_data for YouTube (VIDEO_ID is the 11 characters after v= or youtu.be/, put it in both places):
widget_javascript (the same for both): widget_style (the same for both): .homepage_settings .hero-bg-video{display:none} #first_container{position:relative;box-shadow:none !important} #first_container > .hero-bg-video{position:absolute !important;top:0;right:0;bottom:0;left:0;z-index:0 !important;overflow:hidden;pointer-events:none;container-type:size} #first_container > .hero-bg-video video{width:100%;height:100%;object-fit:cover;display:block} #first_container > .hero-bg-video iframe{position:absolute;top:50%;left:50%;width:177.78vh;height:56.25vw;min-width:100%;min-height:100%;width:max(100cqw,177.78cqh);height:max(100cqh,56.25cqw);max-width:none;transform:translate(-50%,-50%);border:0;opacity:0;transition:opacity 1.2s} #first_container > .hero-bg-video.is-on iframe{opacity:1} #first_container > .hero-bg-video::after{content:"";position:absolute;top:0;right:0;bottom:0;left:0;background:rgba(0,0,0,.45)} #first_container > .container{position:relative;z-index:1} The tint is the ::after rule: set its colour (homepage_bg_overlay_color at homepage_bg_overlay_transparency keeps the site's own overlay). Keep the script and the YouTube URL parameters exactly: the script finds the layer by its class anywhere in the hero, keeps one layer when the hero prints the widget twice (a hero with a form), and shows a YouTube frame only while YouTube draws nothing over it. A Vimeo or Wistia iframe takes the YouTube iframe's place and is shown at once. Nothing else is needed: no page CSS, no z-index on the text.

blocks.title: Search Box Design
blocks.css: BD's settings CSS: box .homepage_settings .search_box; heading .homepage_settings h2 (custom_38); labels .homepage_settings .search_box label (custom_39); button .btn_home_search. A single-class selector loses to these. The box around the search: custom_32 0 hides its background and search_box_padding 0 removes its padding, so the search lines up with the hero headline. The form and fields depend on the hero type: see the css of hero.cta. Restyling the search fields (shape, labels, icons, spacing) needs no widget edit. Call updatePageCss {recipe: "hero.search_box"} once: the tool saves on the Home page 24 rules measured on every hero search form (member and post-type searches, both layouts, desktop and phone, before and after a click, typing, and opening a dropdown or category list). They hide the labels and the icons, give every field and the search button one height and one radius, keep each dropdown arrow and clear button inside its field, and put the fields and the button in even rows of at most four. To change the look, add values with any of: field_background, field_text, field_border, focus_border, focus_ring, arrow (colours as rgb(R, G, B)), height (pixels, default 56), radius (pixels, default 999, 0 for square corners). These looks are off unless the call sends them: joined (the fields and the search button form one piece with one outer border and no border between fields: on screens 992px and wider, a form with up to 4 fields is one oval bar, and a form with 5 or more fields is one rounded card with the fields in rows; in a narrow hero column the card has fewer fields per row; on phones every form is one rounded card with the fields stacked and a thin line between them), dividers (with joined: a short thin line between the fields of the oval bar), shadow (with joined: a soft shadow under the bar or card), field_icons (each field shows its own icon inside it, with no box), button_icon (the search button shows an icon instead of its text: true for a magnifying glass, or the name of any Bootstrap Icons icon, such as arrow-right), button_text (true: the button keeps its text beside the icon). Each call saves the whole look: a value the call leaves out goes back to its default. Do not edit or remove the recipe's rules: each rule covers a state the widget code does not show. A look the values do not cover is added with updatePageCss rules after the recipe: start each selector with #first_container form:has(.btn_home_search), and end the part that names a field or the button with :not(#_):not(#__). To change the look again, call the recipe again with new values. To undo, send the result's undo to updatePageCss.

blocks.title: Select Content to Display
blocks.note:
The 15 homepage rows. One template: {row} is the setting that names the section in row N, section_{N}_* are that row's spacing and background. A row with no section hides its other controls in the admin. The stored value for Custom Content 1 differs from its option value on some sites (Homepage Content). To add, move or remove sections send updateDesignSettings home_rows: each section keeps its spacing and background. Empty rows between sections are fine; empty spacing means 40px. The Streaming sections (members, featured members, reviews, categories and one per post type) read the site's records on every page view: a new or edited member or post shows by itself with its current photo, title and link. A widget holding typed-in cards is a fixed copy that never changes. So a request to show recent, latest or featured members or posts of any kind on the homepage is the Streaming section for that record type: place it with home_rows, set it up with its block's settings (how many, per row, which post type, order) and restyle it with updatePageCss on the selectors its block names. Build a widget for such a list only when the user asks for something that section's settings and CSS cannot do, and then the widget queries the records itself; it never holds copied titles, images or links. To show a site widget as a section, set a free Custom Content block (homepage_content_2 to 10) to
[widget=Name]
and place that block with home_rows.
blocks.css: Target a section's row with the Row selector its block's css names, never .homepage-section-N (the row number). Flat row colour: section_N_background. Gradient, image or overlay: homepage-only CSS on that selector with updatePageCss; a background shorthand there replaces the row colour, background-image alone keeps it underneath.
